figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. (A) Typical NPs with a γ-alkylidenebutenolide core. (B) (i)
Enzymatic fusion pattern in tetronate antibiotic biosynthesis and a
hypothesized general route for γ-alkylidenebutenolide assembly. (ii) A
novel γ-alkylidenebutenolide biosynthetic pathway featuring a cascade
reaction catalyzed by the PesD−PesF enzyme pair, resulting in
lactone ring contraction.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Characterization of the biosynthesis of compounds 1−4. (A) The BGC was investigated in this study. (B) The proposed biosynthetic
pathways of 1−4. (C) Metabolic analysis of the heterologous expression of the pes BGC in A. oryzae. (D) In vitro enzymatic assays catalyzed by
PesG. (E) In vitro enzymatic assays catalyzed by PesD (wild type) and PesF.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. (A) Predicted relative free energy profile (in kcal/mol) for the proposed mechanism from Int-2 (RCe) to 6a (PCe). Computational
method: B3LYP-D3(bj)/def2-TZVP. (B) Predicted substrate binding site of Int-2 in PesF and its mutants based on the holo-form structure. The
distances between C2 of Int-2 and the carboxylate oxygen of Glu are illustrated by dashed lines: <3 Å in the active mutant E99A/P132E and ∼8.6
Å in the inactive mutant E99A/L112E. (C) LC−MS analysis of enzymatic reactions catalyzed by PesD and PesF mutants.
